title: Quantitative Aptitude
description: Build speed and confidence with arithmetic, ratios, percentages, and work-rate questions.
heroText: Practice the most common quant topics asked in aptitude and placement rounds.

topics.title: Percentages, Profit and Loss
topics.summary: Revise percentage change, discount, selling price, and profit-loss conversions.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an item at Rs. 800 and gives a 10% discount. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: 10% of 800 is 80, so the selling price is 720.

questions.question: If the cost price of an article is Rs. 500 and the profit is 20%, what is the selling price?
questions.explanation: 20% of 500 is 100, so selling price is 600.

questions.question: A number increases from 240 to 300. What is the percentage increase?
An item is sold at Rs. 450 with a loss of 10%. What is its cost price?
questions.explanation: If SP is 90% of CP, then CP = 450 / 0.9 = 500.

topics.title: Ratio and Proportion
topics.summary: Practice sharing quantities, comparing values, and solving direct proportion questions.

questions.question: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3:2. If there are 30 boys, how many girls are there?
questions.explanation: 3 parts = 30, so 1 part = 10 and girls = 20.

questions.question: If A:B = 4:5 and B:C = 10:11, then A:C is
questions.explanation: Scale 4:5 to 8:10. Then A:C = 8:11.

questions.question: A sum is divided between X and Y in the ratio 7:3. If Y gets Rs. 900, the total is
questions.explanation: 3 parts = 900, so 10 parts = 3,000.

questions.question: Which pair is in proportion?
questions.explanation: 4/6 and 8/12 are both 2/3.

topics.title: Time and Work
topics.summary: Strengthen work-rate logic for individual and combined productivity questions.

questions.question: A can complete a job in 10 days. What fraction of work does A complete in one day?
questions.explanation: Daily work = 1/10.

questions.question: A can do work in 12 days and B in 18 days. In how many days can they finish it together?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36, so time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.question: If 8 workers finish a task in 15 days, how many days will 10 workers take?
questions.explanation: Workers x days is constant, so 8 x 15 = 10 x d. d = 12.

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. If B takes 18 days, A takes
questions.explanation: Twice efficiency means half the time, so 9 days.

title: Data Interpretation
description: Decode tables, charts, and trends quickly to answer calculation-heavy exam questions.
heroText: Learn how to compare datasets and spot trends without wasting time in exams.

topics.title: Table Analysis
topics.summary: Read row-column data carefully and answer percentage, difference, and ranking questions.

questions.question: A table shows sales of 120, 150, 180, and 210 units in four quarters. Which quarter had the highest sales?
questions.explanation: 210 is the highest value, so Q4 is highest.

questions.question: From the values 80, 100, 120, and 140, what is the average?
If production rises from 250 to 300 units, the increase is
questions.explanation: Increase is 50, so percentage increase = 20%.

questions.question: If employee count is 240 and 25% are interns, the number of interns is

topics.title: Bar Graph Interpretation
topics.summary: Practice reading bars, comparing heights, and calculating totals and gaps.

questions.question: A bar graph shows monthly revenues of 30, 45, 50, and 35 lakhs. Which month is second highest?
questions.explanation: 50 is highest and 45 is second highest.

questions.question: What is the total of values 15, 25, 35, and 45 shown in the graph?
If one bar is 80 and another is 64, what percent is the second of the first?
Values increase from 40 to 52. The increase is
questions.explanation: Increase is 12, so 12/40 x 100 = 30%.

topics.title: Pie Chart Reasoning
topics.summary: Convert sectors to percentages and absolute values quickly.

questions.question: A pie chart sector of 90 degrees represents what percent of the whole?
If 30% of a pie chart represents 150 students, total students are
questions.explanation: 150 is 30%, so total = 500.

questions.question: A category has a 72-degree sector. Its share is
Which angle corresponds to 15% of a pie chart?
questions.explanation: 15% of 360 is 54 degrees.

title: Logical Reasoning
description: Sharpen pattern recognition, arrangement, coding-decoding, and deduction skills.
heroText: Train your mind to identify relationships and solve logic puzzles with structure.

topics.title: Coding-Decoding
topics.summary: Find letter, number, and substitution patterns in encoded words and phrases.

questions.question: If CAT is coded as DBU, how is DOG coded in the same pattern?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one step ahead: D->E, O->P, G->H.

questions.question: If A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, then BAD equals
If APPLE is coded as ELPPA, the pattern used is
questions.explanation: The letters are written in reverse order.

questions.question: Which coding rule best explains DOG -> EPH?
questions.explanation: Every letter advances by one.

topics.title: Seating Arrangement
topics.summary: Practice linear and circular arrangement logic using clue-based elimination.

questions.question: If A sits to the immediate right of B in a row, which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: If A is right of B, then B is left of A.

questions.question: In a circular arrangement, all face the center. The person to your right is in which direction?
questions.explanation: Facing the center flips the usual direction, so right becomes anticlockwise.

questions.question: Five people sit in a row. The middle position is
questions.explanation: In five places, the 3rd seat is central.

questions.question: If two people sit at the extreme ends of a row of six seats, how many seats are between them?
questions.explanation: Seats 2, 3, 4, and 5 are between the two ends.

topics.title: Syllogism
topics.summary: Strengthen conclusion-based reasoning from statements involving classes and sets.

questions.question: All cats are animals. Some animals are pets. Which conclusion definitely follows?
questions.explanation: Only the original universal statement definitely follows.

questions.question: Some pens are pencils. All pencils are wooden. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: Pens that are pencils must also be wooden.

questions.question: No books are tables. All tables are furniture. Which conclusion is valid?
questions.explanation: If no books are tables, then no tables are books.

questions.question: All roses are flowers. All flowers are plants. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: Roses are flowers and flowers are plants, so roses are plants.

title: Verbal Reasoning
description: Improve grammar, vocabulary, inference, and sentence flow for aptitude tests.
heroText: Practice context clues, correct sentence structures, and language-based reasoning.

topics.title: Synonyms and Antonyms
topics.summary: Sharpen vocabulary by identifying close meanings and opposite meanings quickly.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'Rapid'.
questions.explanation: Rapid means quick or fast.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'Expand'.
questions.explanation: Contract is the opposite of expand.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'Elegant'.
questions.explanation: Elegant means graceful or stylish.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'Ancient'.
questions.explanation: Modern is opposite in meaning to ancient.

topics.title: Sentence Improvement
topics.summary: Spot grammar, usage, and structure errors and choose the best correction.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence: 'She do not like coffee.'
questions.explanation: With 'she', the correct form is 'does not like'.

questions.question: Identify the best correction: 'He is senior than me.'
options: He is more senior than me.
questions.explanation: The standard phrase is 'senior to'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'Each of the players ___ ready.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Select the best correction for: 'I look forward to meet you.'
options: I look forward to meeting you.
I look forward for meeting you.
I look forward to met you.
questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' takes a gerund: meeting.

topics.title: Para Jumbles
topics.summary: Organize scrambled sentences into logical order by tracking flow and connectors.

questions.question: Which sentence usually works best as an opening sentence in a paragraph?
questions.explanation: The opening sentence generally introduces the topic.

questions.question: A sentence starting with 'Therefore' should usually come
questions.explanation: 'Therefore' signals a conclusion.

questions.question: Pronouns like 'this' or 'they' often indicate that the sentence
questions.explanation: Pronouns refer back to earlier ideas or nouns.

questions.question: Which clue is most helpful for arranging para jumbles?
questions.explanation: Connectors and references reveal the paragraph flow.
